outline_section.learning_goal: Recognize why sloped signal segments make direct convolution depend on rewriting each overlapping piece as a function of tau before integrating.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach that sloped convolution is still overlap-area convolution, but the integrand now changes with tau because at least one overlapping signal value is linear rather than constant.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use one ramp segment of x(tau) overlapping one constant segment of h(t - tau) over a single interval.
paragraph_plan: Start from the familiar convolution integral and identify tau as the variable being integrated while t is held fixed.
Explain that rectangular-pulse convolution only required overlap length, but a sloped segment requires the actual formula for the signal value at each tau.
Use the signal plot to name the fixed support of x(tau), the shifted support of h(t - tau), and the overlap interval where the product is nonzero.
Show the simplest sloped-times-constant setup and state that the rest of the lesson will build from rewriting segments, to bounds, to integrals, to piecewise assembly.
display_math_plan: Display the convolution integral y(t) = integral x(tau) h(t - tau) d tau.
Display a simple overlap setup such as x(tau) = tau on 0 <= tau <= 1 and h(t - tau) = 1 on t - 1 <= tau <= t.
Display the resulting single-region integral form y(t) = integral_a^b tau d tau, with a and b described as overlap bounds.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: For a finite-duration ramp x(tau) and a finite-duration impulse response h(t - tau), the active convolution regions have been reduced to integrals for each t-interval. Assemble the resulting formulas, including no-overlap intervals, into y(t).
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Produce one complete piecewise definition of y(t) by placing each evaluated convolution contribution on its correct t-interval and adding zero regions outside the total support.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from evaluating one active region to organizing all active and inactive regions into the final LTI system output.
solution_step_plan: List the t-intervals in increasing order.
Mark the no-overlap intervals where y(t) = 0.
Place each evaluated integral result on its corresponding active interval.
Check that the intervals cover the full output support without gaps or overlaps.
Write the final piecewise y(t).
practice_variation_axes: Vary the number of active regions between two and three.
Provide some evaluated region formulas and require assembly only.
Include endpoint shifts so the support of y(t) is not symmetric around zero.

outline_section.handoff_notes: The example writer may reuse results from earlier-style regional integrals, but should not create a long algebra grind. The instructional focus is correct piecewise organization.

prompt_blocks.text: The regional calculations for a sloped convolution give: no overlap for t < -1, contribution (t + 1)^2/2 for -1 <= t < 0, contribution 1/2 for 0 <= t < 1, contribution (2 - t)^2/2 for 1 <= t <= 2, and no overlap for t > 2. Assemble the complete piecewise output y(t).

answer_explanation_blocks.text: Keep the intervals ordered, place each evaluated contribution on its matching active region, and add zero for the two no-overlap regions.

images.lesson_core_move: Evaluate direct convolution involving sloped signal segments by expressing the overlapping pieces in tau, setting time-dependent bounds, and integrating the resulting products.
images.section_title: Assembling the Piecewise Result for Sloped Convolution
images.image_description: A compact assembly diagram for a finite-duration sloped convolution. Show a horizontal t-axis with ordered regions t < 0, 0 <= t < 1, 1 <= t < 2, 2 <= t <= 3, and t > 3. Mark t < 0 and t > 3 as no overlap with y(t) = 0. For the active regions, include a small table or timeline labels: 0 <= t < 1 has tau-overlap 0 <= tau <= t and contribution t^3/6; 1 <= t < 2 has tau-overlap t - 1 <= tau <= t and contribution 1/6; 2 <= t <= 3 has tau-overlap t - 1 <= tau <= 2 and contribution (3 - t)^3/6. Include a final cue reading assemble into y(t). Keep the visual organized as task data, not decorative signal art.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A compact set of signal plots or an overlap timeline showing the time regions for a finite-duration sloped convolution and the corresponding tau-overlap intervals.
visual_elements: input and impulse-response signal plots with simple finite supports
time-region markers for no overlap, growing overlap, full/changed overlap, and shrinking overlap
tau-bound summary for each active region
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Keep the visual organized as a setup aid. Do not ask for plotted answer choices; the answer is a symbolic piecewise expression.

question_policy.answer_format: A piecewise expression for y(t), including zero outside the support and formulas on each active time interval.
question_policy.practice_question_model: Given a finite ramp x(tau) and a finite constant or ramp h(t - tau) with the region integrals already set up, assemble the complete piecewise expression for y(t).
distractor_plan: No answer choices; validate equivalent piecewise forms and interval endpoint conventions.
Common generated wrong-answer patterns should include omitting zero regions, assigning a region formula to the wrong t-interval, or leaving overlapping cases unordered.
